title: Graphing a Vertically and Horizontally Shifted Square Root
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = 1 + sqrt(x - 1) by identifying its parent function, shifts, domain, range, and key points.

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Translations
steps.explanation: Start with the parent graph y = sqrt(x), shift it right 1 unit by replacing x with x - 1, and shift it up 1 unit by adding 1.
steps.why: In y = f(x - h) + k, h = 1 gives a rightward shift of 1 and k = 1 gives an upward shift of 1.

steps.title: Determine the Domain and Range
steps.explanation: The radicand requires x >= 1, and adding 1 to the non-negative square root yields outputs in [1, infinity).
steps.why: The endpoint (0, 0) of y = sqrt(x) translates by (1, 1) to become the minimum point (1, 1).

steps.title: Plot Key Points on the Shifted Curve
steps.explanation: The curve starts at its left endpoint (1, 1) in the first quadrant (with no x- or y-intercepts) and rises smoothly to the right through (2, 2) and (5, 3).
steps.why: Since x >= 1 and y >= 1, the graph lies strictly in the first quadrant and never intersects the coordinate axes.
